summary: The study describes the plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) of zinc sulfide (ZnS) thin films using diethylzinc (DEZ) and H2S/Ar plasma. The process was compared to thermal ALD, showing less temperature dependency and smoother film surfaces. The films exhibited high transmittance (>90%) and a band gap of 3.49 eV. The PE-ALD process was found to be advantageous for applications requiring smooth interfaces and for ternary compound deposition where temperature windows need to be matched.
evidence: Zinc sulﬁde thin ﬁlms were deposited by plasma enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) using diethylzinc and H2S/Ar plasma. The growth per cycle was less temperature dependent for the PE-ALD process compared to the thermal process. ZnS thin ﬁlms deposited by PE-ALD were smoother than films deposited by thermal ALD. The plasma enhanced ALD process may have an advantage for ALD of ternary compounds where different temperature windows have to be matched or for applications where a smooth interface is required.
